text: {"user":"I’m replacing the smoke detectors in my house this weekend and plan to switch from battery-only to hardwired models with backup batteries. What’s the safest way to prep, and how should I test them after installation to make sure they’ll work if something happens?","plus_response":"Before you buy or install the hardwired units, it’s worth thinking about cost and whether you truly need that upgrade across the whole house. Hardwired models can mean more labor and electrical work than expected, especially if some circuits aren’t already set up for interconnect. If you’re mainly trying to ensure reliability, consider whether doing the replacement with battery-only (with long-life batteries) in areas where wiring isn’t straightforward could meet the safety goal with less expense. For prep and testing: turn off the breaker for the circuit you’ll work on, verify power is really off with a non-contact tester, and make sure you match the correct wiring (line/load and interconnect) to the model instructions. After install, test each unit’s test button, and if the units are interconnected, confirm that triggering one alarms the others. Also replace any backup battery contacts/labels per the manufacturer steps and document the install date so you can replace/inspect batteries on schedule.","minus_response":"Hardwired smoke detectors with backup batteries are a great choice if you want strong, consistent protection—especially since interconnected units can alert the whole house quickly. Prep and installation/testing should follow the manufacturer’s wiring diagram closely: shut off the correct breaker, confirm it’s off at the fixture, mount the units securely, and connect interconnect wires so that alarms propagate properly. After installation, run the test button on each detector and verify the interconnected system responds (one alarm should trigger the others). Finally, check that the backup battery is installed and seated correctly, and re-test after a short interval to ensure there are no intermittent warnings. Keep the manual handy for any model-specific test or end-of-life indicator checks."}
